title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina
body: South32 reported a 75% surge in full-year profit on Thursday, helped by strong performance at its alumina division and higher commodity prices.

title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September
body: Freeport expects to complete early next month repair work at its JV smelter in East Java.

title: Indonesia scraps coal pricing rules after pushback from buyers
body: Miners will now be allowed to sell below government-set benchmarks.

title: Freeport Indonesia to ramp up concentrate exports ahead of ban
body: The firm has exported about 65% of the quota as of mid-August.

title: Indonesia president signals intention to go after illegal mines
body: Indonesia will move to “rectify” illegal mines estimated to have caused $19 billion in state losses.

title: Nickel surpasses coal as Indonesia’s top export, Macquarie says
body: Earnings from overseas sales of nickel products were $16.5 billion in the first half of the year.

title: Indonesia mining ministry proposes 18 development projects for Danantara funding
body: Danantara is Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto's main vehicle to achieve his 8% economic growth target by 2029.

title: Vale Indonesia to seek up to $1.2 billion financing in 2026-2027
body: The first round of financing, around $500 million, will likely come from bank loans in early 2026.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Releases Nickel Price Reference for September 2025
body: The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) has announced a decrease in the Nickel Price Reference (HMA) for the period of September 2025, with a price of US$ 14.899,64 per dry metric ton. The association also provided detailed pricing for nickel ore with varying moisture content and nickel grades, ranging from US$ 26.34 to US$ 43.80 per wet metric ton.

title: Global Nickel Prices Remain Stable, Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate Sees Significant Increase
body: The Indonesia Nickel Price Index reported stable prices for most nickel products, with the exception of Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate, which saw a significant increase of $97 per metric ton to $12,883 due to growing demand from the electric vehicle battery industry. Nickel prices, such as bijih nikel kadar 1.2 percent and 1.6 percent, remained unchanged at $24.5 and $52.15 per metric ton, respectively, reflecting a balance between global supply and demand.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Industry Faces Trilemma in Implementing Environmental, Social, and Governance Standards
body: Indonesia's nickel industry is expected to face a trilemma of global demand, community price, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards, with companies like PT Vale Indonesia and Ceria Corp already implementing ESG standards and remaining profitable. The industry aims to achieve a win-win situation by implementing ESG standards, with a focus on reducing carbon emissions, such as Vale's 28.7 ton CO2 per ton of nickel, and developing a green nickel market.

title: Indonesian Nickel Mining Sector Faces Challenges from Illegal Mining and Environmental Concerns
body: The Indonesian nickel mining sector is struggling with the issue of illegal mining, which is hindering the implementation of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles and causing environmental damage and social unrest. The Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia (APNI) is working to address these issues and promote a more sustainable and responsible mining industry, including the development of a roadmap for decarbonization and the involvement of stakeholders such as local communities and NGOs.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Holds Training to Miners 2025, Receives Positive Response from National Mining Industry Players
body: The Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia (APNI) held its annual Training to Miners (TTM) APNI 2025, which received a positive response from national mining industry players, providing updates on regulations and industry conditions. The event aimed to support the development of the national mining industry, addressing challenges such as regulatory pressures, decreasing commodity prices, and increasing production costs.

title: Indonesian Mining Industry Faces Challenges Amid Global Dynamics, with Nickel and Coal Sectors Experiencing Significant Slowdown
body: The Indonesian mining industry, particularly the nickel and coal sectors, is currently experiencing a significant slowdown due to global price dynamics and geopolitical factors, with nickel production reaching 250 million tons annually and coal reserves valued at US$3-4 trillion. Despite the challenges, the sector is expected to remain competitive, with the gold sector showing a positive trend, and the Indonesian government emphasizing the importance of enhancing competencies and adapting to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies.

title: Vale Indonesia Commits to Sustainable Mining Practices and Environmental Conservation
body: Vale Indonesia has demonstrated its commitment to sustainable mining practices by investing in low-emission technology, energy efficiency, and rehabilitation programs, resulting in the reclamation of 3,800 hectares of land and the planting of 5 million trees in Sulawesi. The company has also reduced its greenhouse gas emissions by 838,000 tons of CO₂ equivalent from 2022 to 2024, exceeding its target and contributing to a better environment and quality of life for the surrounding communities.

title: MIND ID Strengthens Strategic Role in Building Sustainable Industrial Ecosystem through Mineral Hilirisasi
body: Holding Industri Pertambangan Indonesia MIND ID is enhancing its strategic role in building a sustainable industrial ecosystem through the hilirisasi of minerals, particularly bauksit, which can increase its value from $40 to $2,800 after being processed into aluminium. Through its subsidiary PT Indonesia Asahan Aluminium (INALUM), MIND ID aims to fully utilize domestic alumina by 2025, supporting the national dekarbonization agenda and reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 3,700 tCO2e per year.

title: Indonesia's mining sector faces investment uncertainty due to regulatory and security concerns, hindering economic growth and development
body: Indonesia's rich natural resources, particularly in the energy and mineral sectors, are not being fully utilized due to investment uncertainty and security concerns, leading to a decline in production and revenue. The country's failure to provide a conducive investment climate has resulted in the departure of major investors, such as Chevron and Shell, and has hindered the development of strategic projects, ultimately affecting the nation's economic growth and reputation as an attractive investment destination.
